Does WhatsApp remove photo metadata? What gets sent and how to be sure

It depends on how you send it. As a normal photo, WhatsApp recompresses the image and drops most metadata. As a document, it sends the original file untouched — GPS location included. Here is how to be sure.

Updated 2026-11-22 · 4 min read
Clean your files in secondsFree, no sign-up, and everything runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
Open IA Cleaner

Sent as a photo

When you send an image the usual way (gallery or camera), WhatsApp makes a new, compressed copy. That copy normally loses most EXIF data, including the GPS location and the camera model, and any C2PA Content Credentials. Quality is reduced too, even with the HD option.

Sent as a document

When you attach the image as a document to keep full quality, WhatsApp sends the original file byte for byte. Everything inside it travels too: GPS location, phone model, dates, editing apps and AI metadata.

Other apps work differently

  • Telegram: “photo” is compressed; “file” sends the original with all its metadata.
  • Email, cloud links and AirDrop: usually send the original file.
  • Social networks: most strip metadata from the public copy, but read it first when you upload.

Clean the photo before sending it

  1. Open iacleaner.com → Images in your phone’s browser.
  2. Pick the photo, check what it contains, and tap Download clean image.
  3. Send the clean copy, as a photo or as a document — full quality, no metadata.

Nothing is uploaded: the photo is cleaned on your phone.

Can you see the metadata of a photo you received?

If it came as a normal WhatsApp photo, there is usually little left besides basic size information. If it came as a document, drop it into IA Cleaner to see everything it contains.
